sections.h2: Who records deeds in Adams County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Adams County Recorder of Deeds records them, from an office in the Adams County Courthouse at 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, in Gettysburg. Staff answer at 717-337-9826 on weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., and the office shuts for every holiday on the county calendar.

Recordings stop at 4:00 p.m., half an hour before the doors close, so a closing package that arrives at 4:20 waits for the next business day. The same office acts as the Department of Revenue's agent for realty transfer tax and hands the money on to the state, the municipality and the school district.

Anyone selling a house in Adams County meets this office at the very end of the sale: the deed is signed at closing, then recorded here, and the recording date is when the new owner shows up in the public record.

sections.h2: What does the Adams County recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A deed or a mortgage costs $71.25 to record under the fee bill that took effect December 1, 2025. That covers the first four pages and the first four names, and a few add-ons apply after that.

Adams County Recorder of Deeds fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025
Document or itemFee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Each page over 4 (deed or mortgage)$4.00
Each name over 4 (deed or mortgage)$1.00
Satisfaction piece or mortgage release$61.75
Assignment of mortgage$61.75
Easement or right of way$59.75
Power of attorney$18.50
Copies, per page$0.25

Source: the county's Recording Fee Bill. The schedule says that if a document type carries no listed fee, the Recorder of Deeds sets one, and it adds that all fees are payable at the time of recording.

Payment for the recording fee can be cash, check, or a debit or credit card, though a vendor fee is added to card payments. The office cannot make change on a check, so an overpayment of $10 or less is kept as an overpayment and shows that way on the receipt. Anything above $10 means a new check.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax paid when a house sells in Adams County?
sections.html:
Check only, with no cash taken, at the moment the deed is recorded. The county's fee bill describes a 1% state tax plus a local tax of the same amount, and it calls for three separate checks: one to the state, one to the township or borough, and one for the recording fee.

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue explains that buyer and seller are both liable for the tax. Its page also lists transfers that escape the tax, such as certain family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy.

  • A Statement of Value is required whenever the tax is not paid in full, including when a family exemption is claimed.
  • When land lies in two or more municipalities, the deed has to state how the value splits so the local share goes to the right place.
  • The county's fee bill lists grandparent to grandchild and sibling transfers among the exemptions it recognizes.
  • A Certificate of Residence has to be completed and signed on every deed and mortgage before the office will record it.

The Statement of Value is a Revenue form with no recording charge at this office, and the county directs people with questions on it to the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: What paperwork rules does the Adams County office enforce?
sections.html:
Documents must relate to real estate, carry original signatures, and be properly notarized. The date on the document cannot come after the date of the notary acknowledgment.

Adams County stands apart from many Pennsylvania counties on a few points. It does not use the Uniform Parcel Identifier system, so no UPI fee is collected and no parcel number or street address is required on a document being recorded. It also sets no margin rules, and it takes both letter and legal size paper.

  • Include a self-addressed stamped envelope; finished documents are mailed back about two weeks after the recording date.
  • Assignments of mortgage must cite the book and page of the original mortgage.
  • Subdivision plans must be 18 by 24 inches, signed by the township or borough and the county planning commission, and recorded within 90 days of approval.
  • Remote online notarization is accepted only during a declared emergency.

sections.h2: How can I get a document to the Adams County recorder?
sections.html:
There are three routes: an in-person visit, the secure drop box outside the courthouse entrance, or mail by USPS, FedEx or UPS. Appointments are preferred but not required, and they can be made by phone or by email to registerrecorder@adamscountypa.gov.

The courthouse lobby has public terminals for searching records, and a copier that runs on a button picked up from the Register and Recorder or the Prothonotary. There is no terminal inside the recording office itself, and photographing screens, books or microfilm is prohibited.

The office also runs a free fraud alert service called PropertyCheck, which emails or texts an owner whenever a document is recorded against their property. A seller who plans to hold other property in the county may find that useful.

Ask the recorder whether a title company can send a closing package electronically, because the office pages open to the public describe paper, drop box and mail only.

sections.h2: What does Adams County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Adams County covers about 522 square miles in south central Pennsylvania, and Gettysburg sits at the center of it, ringed on three sides by the national military park. Thirteen historic roads meet at or near the borough, and most of the farmland outside it has kept its nineteenth century layout.

The Census Bureau estimated 107,594 residents in July 2025, up 3.6% from the 2020 base, while Allegheny and Armstrong counties both lost residents over the same stretch.

With a median home value of $268,500 and nearly four in five households owning, most sales here are owner to owner. The county also lists a Tax Services office among its recording resources, which a new owner can contact after the deed is on record.

sections.h2: What should I have ready before closing in Adams County?
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps a deed from bouncing at the counter.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the notary's venue, expiration date and a legible stamp.
  • Three checks drawn on the correct accounts: state tax, local tax and recording fee, with the amounts matching the deed's stated consideration.
  • A completed Certificate of Residence and, if any tax is excused, a filled-in Statement of Value.
  • A stamped return envelope addressed to the new owner or the title agent.
  • Arrival before the 4:00 p.m. cutoff on a weekday that is not a county holiday.

Whoever delivers the deed to the courthouse, the same steps apply, so agree before closing on who will carry the package in and who gets the recorded original back.

faqs.q: What is the base recording fee for a deed in Adams County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $71.25 for a deed or mortgage under the schedule effective December 1, 2025, plus $4.00 for each page after the fourth and $1.00 for each name after the fourth. Transfer tax is paid separately, by check.

faqs.q: When does Adams County stop accepting documents each day?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 4:00 p.m. on business days, even though the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. For a special circumstance the office asks you to call or email before you come.

faqs.q: Is cash accepted for transfer tax at the Adams County courthouse?
faqs.a: No. Realty transfer tax must be paid by check, and the office asks for separate checks for the state tax, the local tax and the recording fee. Recording fees themselves can be paid in cash or by card with a vendor fee.

faqs.q: Must a deed carry a parcel number to be recorded here?
faqs.a: No. The county does not use the UPI system, and a parcel identification number or property address is not required on documents submitted for recording. A Certificate of Residence is required, though.

faqs.q: Where should a signed deed be delivered or mailed?
faqs.a: Send it to the Recorder of Deeds at the Adams County Courthouse, 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, Gettysburg, PA 17325, or use the drop box at the entrance. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope; return mail takes about two weeks.
